title: Dipole Gravitational Waves and a Weak Stochastic Vector-Field Background
content: In linearized general relativity, the metric perturbation tensor projected onto an observer’s local rest frame transforms the field and force equations into manifestly covariant Maxwell-like vector equations. This 3+1 frame decomposition provides a powerful, intuitive tool for modeling weak-field gravitational interactions, high-speed laboratory tests, and compact-binary dynamics. We show that ordinary quadrupolar radiation from a rotating binary is mathematically and physically equivalent to a linear superposition of Doppler-modulated dipole waves emitted by each mass. In well-behaved binaries, dipole interference is nearly complete; however, nonlinear strong-field disruptions during compact-binary mergers lay bare residual dipole-frequency strain signals. Analysis of the GW150914 strain waveform reveals a fundamental orbit-frequency component at approximately 7 percent of the total amplitude and 0.5 percent of the power. Treating weak-field gravity in a static universe within a Parametrized Post-Newtonian framework implies a cosmic gravitational background (CGB) of spin-1 gravitons in thermal equilibrium at 20 to 22 K, relating the Hubble constant directly to Planck’s constant. An exact solution of Einstein’s equations for a static universe with a CGB accounts for the Hubble redshift, mature galaxies at high redshifts, and the appearance of cosmic acceleration in Type Ia supernovas without invoking dark energy.
